parsed.n_justification: The upper Yakima basin spans roughly 500 m valley floors near Cle Elum to >2000 m Cascade crest, a ~1500 m relief that controls a strong snow-rain transition. Five columns place representative points in ~300 m elevation bands (valley, lower montane rain-snow transition, mid montane seasonal snow, upper montane persistent snow, subalpine/crest). This resolves the critical rain-to-snow transition zone (~1000-1500 m) with adequate density while keeping the campaign computationally tractable for single-column runs; fewer would miss the transition band, more would add little given ELM columns are independent and forcing is downscaled to the same reanalysis product.
assumptions: Each column is run independently with no lateral routing; basin integration is diagnostic (post-processing) not dynamic
Atmospheric forcing is elevation-corrected to each column via lapse rate; precipitation phase is set by ELM's air-temperature threshold
A multi-year spin-up (recycling 2000-2020 forcing, ~50-100 yr) precedes the transient run to equilibrate soil moisture, snow, and carbon pools
Vegetation types from satellite/CLM surface data: mixed conifer forest at mid bands, subalpine parkland at crest, shrub-grass at valley
Soil textures assigned from SSURGO/gridded soil data are held vertically representative per column
The 21-year window (2000-2020) captures interannual snow variability including warm/low-snow years
